blocks.title: Keys and values
blocks.what: Each line is a key, then a colon and a space, then its value.
blocks.why: Programs find each value by its key. Kubernetes reads every file this way.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file is empty, so a program reading it finds nothing.
blocks.comment: Three keys, each followed by a colon, a space, and a value

blocks.title: Nesting with two spaces
blocks.what: address has no value on its own line. The lines indented below it belong to address.
blocks.why: Nesting groups related keys together. Kubernetes uses it everywhere, such as metadata holding a name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without the two spaces, city and country stop belonging to address. YAML reads them as separate top-level keys.
blocks.comment: address holds two keys, each indented by two spaces
blocks.yaml:
name: Asha
course: Kubernetes
batch: 10
address:
  city: Hyderabad
  country: India

mistake.yaml:
name: Asha
course: Kubernetes
batch: 10
address:
  city: Hyderabad
   country: India
mistake.error: yaml: line 6: mapping values are not allowed in this context
mistake.explain: country has three spaces, one more than city. YAML reads it as part of the value Hyderabad, where a colon is not allowed.
mistake.fix: Line up country with city, two spaces from the left.

blocks.title: A list with dashes
blocks.what: Each line starting with a dash and a space is one item. skills holds a list of two items.
blocks.why: A list holds several values under one key. Kubernetes uses lists for containers, ports, and volumes.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without the dashes, YAML joins the lines into one text value: Linux Docker.
blocks.comment: skills is a list. Each dash starts one item
blocks.yaml:
name: Asha
course: Kubernetes
batch: 10
address:
  city: Hyderabad
  country: India
skills:
  - Linux
  - Docker

blocks.title: A list of nested items
blocks.what: Each dash starts one item, and each item holds its own keys. The second key lines up under the first.
blocks.why: Kubernetes lists containers this way. Each container is one item with its own name and image.
blocks.ifRemoved: If tool moves left to line up with the dash, YAML reports an error and rejects the file.
blocks.comment: projects is a list. Each item has its own name and tool
blocks.yaml:
name: Asha
course: Kubernetes
batch: 10
address:
  city: Hyderabad
  country: India
skills:
  - Linux
  - Docker
projects:
  - name: website
    tool: Docker
  - name: cluster
    tool: Kubernetes

notes.name: A key with the text value Asha.
notes.course: A key with the text value Kubernetes.
notes.batch: A key with the number 10 as its value.
notes.address: A key with no value on its line. The indented lines below are its value.
notes.address.city: Nested under address, because it is indented two spaces more.
notes.address.country: Also nested under address. It lines up exactly with city.
notes.skills: A key whose value is a list.
notes.skills[]: One list item. A dash and a space start it.
notes.projects: A key whose value is a list of items, each with its own keys.
notes.projects[].name: The first key of a list item. The dash before it starts a new item.
notes.projects[].tool: Another key in the same item. It lines up with name, not with the dash.

questions.question: What is the value of city?
questions.explain: city sits two spaces inside address. Its value is Hyderabad.

questions.question: How many items are in the skills list?
answers: None, because skills is a key
questions.explain: Each line that starts with a dash is one list item. skills has two.

questions.question: What does each item under projects hold?
questions.explain: The dash starts an item. name and tool line up under it, so both belong to that item.

fix.message: yaml: line 13: could not find expected ':'
fix.explain: A key needs a colon and a space before its value. The reader reports line 13, where it notices.
